newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUBA'S ZEITLER WARNS AGAINST LAX VIEW OF EMU RULES.
newsitem.headline: BUBA'S ZEITLER WARNS AGAINST LAX VIEW OF EMU RULES.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Friday that a strict interpretation of Maastricht criteria was key to the success of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
A lax approach would threaten the euro's stability, he said in a summary of a speech prepared for delivery in Duesseldorf.
Zeitler warned specifically against a "generous" reading of the criterion for euro hopefuls to reduce budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year.
"Credibility in the fulfilment of fiscal criteria is important for the long-term stability and a long-term acceptance of the euro," Zeitler said.
He said the three percent target had become an international benchmark by which to judge the fiscal policy and stability outlook of a country.

The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) forecast in a report on Thursday that Germany, Italy and France would fail to meet the 3.0 deficit target, achieving deficit-to-GDP ratios of 3.2 percent in 1997.

Zeitler, who is also president of the Bavarian state central bank, added that a clear fulfilment of Maastricht rules should also be seen in the context of the stability pact, due to be signed at a summit of European leaders in Amsterdam next week.
The pact, designed to ensure budgetary discipline after the birth of the euro planned for January 1999, contains sanctions to be imposed on countries which breach reference limits, he said.
Such details should not leave room for interpretation "after the decimal point," he said.
